parsed.explanation: The quoted sentence appears verbatim and is literal placeholder text ('(something that forces)'). In the subcase μ>τ, the required bound D(P∪R) ≤ μ−1 is never established: the padding argument does not show P∪R∪{dummy} is a refinement of B_{n−1} by ≤ n−1 cuts, the identity ∫₀^τ δ_M = τ − D(P∪R') is asserted, and 'the identity D_rest = μ−1 in the worst case' is circular and garbled (note ∑(P∪R) = S_n − μ > μ − 1, so even the trivial bound is insufficient). The subcase with all Q-pieces ≤ τ uses an uncounted 'virtual' cut, misapplies the inductive hypothesis to halves of length 2^{n−1} (not copies of B_{n−1}, whose total is 2^n − 1), and invokes an unproven parity-lattice claim, then defers to n ≤ 3 checks. The closing remark offers a stronger claim only as 'consistent with numerical data'. Nowhere is Theorem B proved for all n, so the all-n lower-bound obligation is unmet.
